name: Email, SMS and WhatsApp retention (welcome, abandoned cart and browse, post-purchase, win-back, VIP and repeat)
asked_as: customers buy once and never come back
start WhatsApp marketing for my store
post-purchase emails to get a second order
outcome: The flow that adds the most gross profit is built first and in full: segmented by what and when people bought, timed from the store's own reorder gaps and delivery times, any offer inside the margin, written in the brand's voice and language, and handed over ready to load (HTML or Klaviyo-ready) with subject lines, send timing and a holdout that shows what it really adds.
first_principles: For most stores below large scale, retention money sits in the second order, and it is won or lost in the first 30 to 60 days. Time every message from this store's own median and 75th percentile days to second order, per first product, and from its delivery time; a template's '30 days' is a guess.

Choose the flow by its gap, not by a checklist: monthly entrants x (the store's own achievable revenue per recipient minus today's) x gross margin. A store with heavy traffic and no added-to-cart flow should not start with win-back; a store with a large quiet buyer file and steady reorders should.

Attributed email revenue is not extra revenue. Apple privacy inflates opens and a 5-day open window acts like view-through, so judge flows on placed-order rate and revenue per recipient after discount cost, and prove win-back, replenishment and VIP with a 10% holdout.

Discounts teach buyers to wait. The ladder is help first (answers, how-to, proof), then the smallest offer that still leaves gross profit on the returning order, only for people past the reorder gap, with a real expiry. Never open an abandonment flow with a code, and never send sale campaigns to active subscribers.

Segment by what and when they bought: product type (used up or bought once), order count, days since last order against that product's own cycle, gross profit to date, and bad-experience flags (return, complaint, low rating, failed COD delivery). The last group gets a fix-first note, not a promotion.

Inbox placement comes before copy: an authenticated domain, sends to engaged people only, a sunset rule, spam complaints well under 0.3%. Each channel has one job: email for depth, SMS for urgency, WhatsApp for conversation and COD confirmation where buyers live on it, each with consent recorded.

data_map.question: How many first buyers come back, and when?
data_map.data: Second-order rate at 60 and 90 days by first-order month and first product; median and 75th percentile days to second order
data_map.if_missing: the platform's predicted next order date if 500+ buyers; else the returning-customer rate, marked misleading

data_map.question: Which flow has the biggest gap?
data_map.data: Monthly entrants, revenue per recipient and placed-order rate per flow against the store's own best 30 days; trigger volumes for missing flows
data_map.where: flow report; store abandoned checkouts, orders and sign-ups; GA4 add_to_cart
data_map.if_missing: trigger volumes from the store, with half the conversion of the closest existing flow as the planning rate

data_map.question: Is mail reaching the inbox?
data_map.data: Domain authentication, engaged open rate excluding privacy opens, click rate, spam complaints, bounces, engaged share of the list
data_map.where: DNS, Google Postmaster, platform deliverability report
data_map.if_missing: DNS lookup plus open and click trends by month

data_map.question: Who has lapsed, and what were they worth?
data_map.data: Recency, frequency and gross profit per customer; cutoffs from the store's own days between orders
data_map.if_missing: the platform's built-in RFM groups, noting their fixed cutoffs

data_map.question: When does each product run out?
data_map.data: Reorder gaps per product and quantity; pack size and daily use
data_map.if_missing: median reorder gap per product alone

data_map.question: How deep can an offer go?
data_map.data: Delivered cost per product; break-even at each discount depth
data_map.where: SKU costs, shipping, fees, returns, failed COD
data_map.if_missing: no money off; value-add offers only

tools: node tools/ask-knowledge.mjs "<flow> timing, length and offer" --module EML,CXP,OFF
look_for: Second-order rate at 60 and 90 days by first product: products that make repeat buyers should lead the welcome flow and acquisition; one-time products need a cross-sell path, not a reorder reminder.
The shape of the repeat curve: most second orders inside 30 days means post-purchase is the lever; a long, flat tail means replenishment timing or win-back.
Median and 75th percentile days to second order: post-purchase must land before the median; win-back starts past the 75th percentile or about twice the median, not at a fixed 90 days.
Flows earning less than campaigns on a store with steady traffic: usually missing or mis-triggered flows, most often one abandonment flow on Started Checkout and nothing on Added to Cart.
Revenue per recipient per flow against the store's own best 30 days: a fall with steady entrants means the flow broke (trigger, filter, smart sending left on, deliverability), not the copy.
Engaged opens well under about 50% on a 90-day engaged segment, or complaints near 0.3%: fix inbox placement before writing anything new.
Discount dependence: the share of orders with a code and buyers who only buy with one; offers to them in win-back and abandonment mostly give margin away.
Bad-experience buyers in the lapsed pile: returns, complaints, low ratings, failed COD; if they are over about 20% of the lapsed, fix the cause and send a fix-first note.
Timing against delivery: review asks or how-to emails that land before the parcel, order updates carrying promotions, COD orders sent marketing before they are confirmed.
Overlap: one person in welcome, browse, cart and a campaign on the same day; selling flows with no exit on purchase; active subscribers in sale sends.
A small, slow-growing list caps every flow: sign-up rates of 2 to 3% are common and 8 to 12% achievable; phone capture as the form's second step.
A few customers carrying the profit: the top 10 to 20% by gross profit; they need service and early access, not deeper discounts.

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: The second order is the leak
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: a low 60-day second-order rate against the store's best cohort, with post-purchase limited to a thank-you
hypothesis_patterns.bet: a post-purchase sequence timed from the store's median days to second order and delivery time, per first product

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: many add-to-carts by known visitors a month and no Added to Cart flow, or one flow on Started Checkout only
hypothesis_patterns.bet: a separate added-to-cart flow and a full checkout flow, discount held late or not at all

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: many buyers past the 75th percentile reorder gap, no win-back or one generic coupon
hypothesis_patterns.bet: a win-back ladder by value and reason, with a holdout and a sunset step

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: falling engaged opens, rising complaints, sends to the whole list, no sunset
hypothesis_patterns.bet: authenticate, send to engaged only, sunset the dead, then widen slowly

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: consumables with tight, clustered reorder gaps and no reminder
hypothesis_patterns.bet: a replenishment reminder at about 75% of the usage cycle, first one without a discount

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: a high share of orders with codes, campaigns that spike only on sales
hypothesis_patterns.bet: no-discount versions of every flow; value-add offers; codes only for the deeply lapsed

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: A few customers carry the profit
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: the top fifth of customers by gross profit hold most of it
hypothesis_patterns.bet: a VIP flow with early access and service, and an early warning when a VIP slows down

decisions.ask: Build one flow fully, or a light pass across all flows?

options.label: One flow fully
options.pro: segments, every message, texts and a holdout: the deepest gain and a clean read
options.con: other flows wait
options.when: one gap is clearly the largest and the basics work

options.label: A light pass on all
options.pro: fixes triggers, timings and missing flows fast
options.con: thin messages; hard to tell what earned
options.when: the account is broken: core flows missing, on the wrong trigger or never exiting

options.label: Repair basics, then one flow fully
options.pro: stops the leaks this week, then builds the biggest gap
options.con: two rounds of loading
options.when: the audit finds broken basics and one big gap

decisions.recommend: From the account audit and the flow ranking: if any core flow is broken or missing, repair first; then build the largest gap in full. Show the ranking that decided it.

decisions.ask: How should the flow use offers?

options.label: No discounts
options.pro: keeps margin and price trust; answers, proof and story do the work
options.con: slower on the deeply lapsed and on price-led buyers
options.when: thin margins, a high share of code-only buyers, or a premium brand

options.label: An offer ladder
options.pro: help first, then the smallest profitable offer late, with a real expiry
options.con: some buyers learn to wait for the last email
options.when: healthy margins and buyers past the reorder gap

options.label: Value instead of money off
options.pro: a gift, free shipping or early access often costs less than the same discount
options.con: needs a gift buyers want
options.when: the discount ceiling is low but a cheap, wanted add-on exists

decisions.recommend: From the discount ceiling per product, the share of code-only buyers and order value. Name who is excluded from any offer (active subscribers, VIPs in sales, recent full-price buyers).

rules: Every delay comes from the store's own reorder gaps, usage cycles and delivery times; a fixed day count only where no store number exists, and it is marked as a default.
Every selling flow exits on purchase; order and delivery messages carry no promotion.
Each email has one job and one ask; the subject and preview are paid off in the first lines; every template tag has a fallback; the footer has the unsubscribe link and postal address.
Offers come after help, at the smallest depth that passes the gross profit check, with a real expiry; never in the first abandonment message; never to active subscribers in sales.
Bad-experience buyers (return, complaint, low rating, failed delivery) get a fix-first note, not a promotion.
SMS under 160 characters with no emoji; WhatsApp header 60, body 1,024, buttons 25 characters, in the right template category; quiet hours and opt-out wording in every marketing text.
Win-back, replenishment and VIP flows keep a 10% holdout; attributed revenue is always labelled attributed.
Voice, proof and offers come from the brand brain and the store's own reviews, in the brand's language and register, including its mix of languages where it uses one.

checks: Each HTML email renders at 375 and 600 px wide, in dark mode and with images off; every link, button and tag fallback works.
No person can get two marketing messages from different flows on the same day; every flow has its exit and its smart-sending setting written down.
Each offer's depth is at or under that product's discount ceiling, and the excluded groups are named.
senior_review: Is this the flow with the biggest gross profit gap by this store's numbers, and did I show why?
Do the timings come from this store's reorder gaps and delivery times, not a template?
Does every offer leave gross profit on the returning order, and who is kept out of it?
Will these land in the inbox, and is anything going to people who never engage?
Does it read like the brand, with real proof and the customers' own words?
Is there a holdout and a read date, so the owner sees real orders, not attributed revenue?
Is it legal to send: consent recorded, unsubscribe, address, registered sender, quiet hours?

ask: flow length and first delay by flow
offer ladder in abandonment and win-back
US email and text consent rules
India DLT and WhatsApp template rules

never: Voice, product facts, reviews and offers come from the brand brain and the store's data, never from the library.
Benchmark open and click rates are ranges to sanity-check, never this store's target; its own best period is.

files: A flow ranking table: each flow's gross profit gap a month, the numbers behind it, and why this one goes first.
A build spec per flow: trigger, filters, splits (new, returning, VIP, subscriber, COD), delays, exits, smart-sending setting and the exact segment conditions.

Every email as responsive HTML (inline CSS, 600 px, Klaviyo tags with fallbacks) and plain text, each with two subject lines, preview text, send delay and the hypothesis it serves, one folder per flow.
SMS and WhatsApp texts with character counts, template category and send window.
An offer rule sheet: who gets what, in which message, how deep, when it expires, and the gross profit check behind it.
A measurement plan: holdout set-up, the one metric per flow, the read date, and the retention dashboard rows to watch.
next_moves: Build the next flow in the ranking.
A subject line and delay test sized to your list.
A sign-up form that grows the list without giving margin away.
